user_prompt:
In the figure, PQ and RS are intersecting straight lines.

[Image: Intersecting lines PQ and RS]

What is the value of x + y ?

Figure, described in words:
Two straight lines intersect. Line PQ slopes downward from upper-left (point P) to lower-right (point Q). Line RS slopes upward from lower-left (point R) to upper-right (point S). At the intersection, an angle arc indicates the obtuse top angle between ray P and ray S, labeled 150°. An arc indicates the acute angle on the left between ray P and ray R, labeled x°. An arc indicates the acute angle on the right between ray S and ray Q, labeled y°.

A. 15
B. 30
C. 60
D. 180
E. 300

answer.description: The letter of the option you choose for the question.
answer.title: Answer

llm_thinking:
I'm working out the angles formed by two intersecting lines, with the top angle given as 150° and vertical angles equal, trying to figure out how x and y relate at the other positions around the intersection point.

Since PQ is a straight line, angle SOQ must be 180° minus 150°, giving y = 30°. Likewise, since ROS is straight, x = 30° too, so x + y = 60°, pointing to answer C.
